# 1 Enoch Chapter 25 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 25 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 25:1 — God "visiting the earth with goodness" vs. "in goodness" vs. "in blessing"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "visit the earth with goodness" | "With goodness" as instrumental |
| LOGOS | "visit the earth in goodness" | "In goodness" as modal |
| PNEUMA | "visit the earth in blessing" | "Blessing" for "goodness" — more eschatologically loaded |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "visit the earth in goodness." The Ge'ez preposition is modal (the mode of the visit is goodness/beneficence). PNEUMA's "in blessing" reads too specifically as a distinct act of blessing rather than the character of the visitation. EMET's "with goodness" is acceptable but "in goodness" is idiomatic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 25:2 — "no mortal is permitted to touch it"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "no mortal is permitted to touch it" | Literal; "mortal" for 'adam (human being) |
| LOGOS | "no mortal is permitted to touch it" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "no human being may touch it" | "Human being" for mortal; "may" for "is permitted" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three agree in substance. Adopted LOGOS/EMET "no mortal is permitted to touch it." "Mortal" captures the contrast with the eternal tree; "is permitted" preserves the formal prohibition register.

**Status:** No significant disagreement.

---

## 25:4 — "Its fragrance shall be in their bones"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "its fragrance shall be in their bones" | Literal; unusual phrase retained |
| LOGOS | "Its fragrance shall be in their bones" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "The tree's fragrance will fill their very bones" | "Fill" and "very bones" add emphasis |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET "Its fragrance shall be in their bones." The unusual idiom — fragrance penetrating to the bones — is a Semitic expression of profound physical well-being; it should be retained rather than normalized. PNEUMA's "fill" loses the penetrating quality.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 25:4 — longevity promise "such as your fathers lived"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they shall live a long life on earth, such as your fathers lived" | "Fathers" for ancestors |
| LOGOS | "they shall live a long life on earth, such as your fathers lived" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "they will live out long lives on earth — lives as long as your ancestors lived" | "Ancestors" for "fathers"; redundant "lives" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET "your fathers." "Fathers" in this context means the antediluvian patriarchs whose lifespans are recorded in Genesis 5 — a culturally specific term. PNEUMA's "ancestors" is accurate but less precise.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---
